message.content:
Below is a quick‑look calendar of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a public holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day break.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 2–4** | New Year’s Day (observed) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday, Jan 2. |
| **Feb 20–22** | Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan) | Family Day is a provincial holiday; it fell on Monday, Feb 20. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Good Friday is a federal holiday; it fell on Friday, Apr 7. |
| **May 22–24** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day is a federal holiday; it fell on Monday, May 22. |
| **Sep 4–6** | Labour Day | Labour Day is a federal holiday; it fell on Monday, Sep 4. |
| **Oct 9–11** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving is a federal holiday; it fell on Monday, Oct 9. |
| **Dec 25–27** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day is a federal holiday; it fell on Monday, Dec 25. |

> **Quick tip:** If you’re building a holiday‑planning app, you might want to flag the *observed* dates (e.g., Jan 2 for New Year’s Day) as well as the actual holiday dates, because many Canadians will take the day off on the observed date.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the same list for another year or for a specific province!
